claims: Measles is caused by the measles virus.
Measles spreads through airborne droplets.
Measles spreads through coughing, sneezing, or close contact.
The measles virus can live in the air or on surfaces for up to 2 hours.
Infected people can spread the measles virus 4 days before to 4 days after the rash appears.
Symptoms typically appear 7–14 days after exposure to measles.
Initial symptoms of measles include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes.
Initial symptoms of measles include conjunctivitis.
Small white spots known as Koplik spots may appear inside the cheeks as early signs of measles.
The measles rash is red and blotchy.
The measles rash appears 3-5 days after initial symptoms.
The measles rash starts on the face and spreads downward.
The measles rash lasts 5-6 days.
Common complications of measles include ear infections and severe diarrhea.
Severe complications of measles include pneumonia.
Severe complications of measles include encephalitis.
Severe complications of measles include death.
Pneumonia is a common cause of death from measles.
Measles can cause severe complications like pneumonia and encephalitis, especially in children under 5.
High-risk groups for measles complications include children under 5.
High-risk groups for measles complications include adults over 20.
High-risk groups for measles complications include pregnant individuals.
High-risk groups for measles complications include those with weakened immune systems.
The Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR) vaccine is 97% effective.
There is no specific antiviral treatment for measles.
Vaccination is the only effective preventative measure against measles.
As of March 2026, over 1,400 measles cases have been reported in the US this year.
